statement: k-Opt local search for the travelling salesman problem is exact - every k-Opt local optimum is a globally optimal tour - once k is as large as ceil(n/2).
definitions: Symmetric TSP on the complete graph K_n with arbitrary nonnegative edge weights (triangle inequality NOT assumed); a k-change replaces at most k edges of the current tour by other edges to form a new tour; a tour is a k-Opt local optimum if no k-change produces a strictly shorter tour; n = number of cities.
ground_truth_witness: n = 8 cities A..H, symmetric weights: w(AB)=w(BC)=w(DE)=w(FG)=w(HA)=1; w(CD)=w(EF)=w(GH)=0; w(AF)=w(AG)=w(BD)=w(BE)=1; w(CH)=2; every other pair has weight 1000 (a stand-in for infinity). The tour A-B-C-D-E-F-G-H-A has length 1+1+0+1+0+1+0+1 = 5 and is globally optimal. The tour A-F-E-B-D-C-H-G-A has length 1+0+1+1+0+2+0+1 = 6 and is a local optimum for k-change with k = ceil(8/2) = 4: every strictly better tour differs from it in at least 5 edges. So 4-Opt gets stuck at 6 while the optimum is 5.
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records

skeptic.objection: Reference verified by brute force over all 2520 tours on the 8-city instance: global optimum length 5 (A-B-C-D-E-F-G-H), the tour A-F-E-B-D-C-H-G has length 6 and the only strictly better tour differs from it in exactly 5 edges, so it is a 4-Opt (= ceil(8/2)) local optimum that is not global. Claim needs the k-Opt neighbourhood pinned (at most k edges replaced) but is otherwise precise; weights are non-metric (1000 as infinity), which the claim permits. Genuine construction: a solver must design an instance whose only improving tours are far in edge-distance. Not in roster.
skeptic.suggested_definitions: Symmetric TSP on the complete graph K_n with arbitrary nonnegative edge weights (triangle inequality NOT assumed); a k-change replaces at most k edges of the current tour by other edges to form a new tour; a tour is a k-Opt local optimum if no k-change produces a strictly shorter tour; n = number of cities.
